grammar.title: What for? with 干吗
grammar.explanation: 干吗 (gànmá) is a casual way to ask "what for, why" — often showing a bit of surprise or mild complaint about someone's action. It's common in spoken Chinese.

grammar.title: Totaling, altogether with 共有
grammar.pattern: (地方/范围) + 共有 + 数量 + 名词
grammar.explanation: 共有 (gòngyǒu) means "to have a total of, altogether there are" — used when counting up everything in a group. It goes right before the total number and noun.

sentences.zh: 这个班共有三十个学生。
sentences.pinyin: Zhège bān gòngyǒu sānshí gè xuésheng.
sentences.en: This class has thirty students in total.

sentences.zh: 这次比赛共有一百人参加。
sentences.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài gòngyǒu yī bǎi rén cānjiā.
sentences.en: A hundred people took part in this competition in total.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè běn shū gòngyǒu èrshí kè.
sentences.en: This book has twenty lessons in total.
